land.text: the unoccupied Oran province, recognised to Abd al-Qadir by the Treaty of Desmichels in 1834 (and, from 1837, 'approximately two thirds of Algeria')

predecessors.note: The Emirate page lists the Regency of Algiers as its predecessor ('the chaos that spread after the fall of Turkish rule in Algeria'); Cliopatria draws the unoccupied remainder under the Regency's name until 1845.

land.text: the whole country, as Cliopatria's French Algeria row (211,876 km2) draws it from 1846

successors.note: The page gives French Algeria as successor; the Emir surrendered on 23 December 1847 and was held in France until 1852 (conquest page).

capitals.name: Tagdemt (Tahert, near Tiaret)
capitals.note: Infobox: Tagdemt (1835-1847); the page says the fortress 'fell to French invaders' (undated) and the Emir's books went to the Smala, his mobile encampment. The coordinates are the gazetteer's 'Tahert' historic site.

rulers.name: Abd al-Qadir (Emir Abdelkader)
rulers.note: Emir from 27 November 1832 to his surrender on 23 December 1847.

correction.text: the Mascara country around the first capital: 'Mascara (1832-1835)'; the page gives no territory for 1832-1833

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, confidence low: the infobox gives the establishment (27 November 1832) and Mascara as capital but no boundary. Cliopatria has no row for the Emirate and draws this land inside 'Regency of Algiers' (196-208 k km2). The Mascara province (admin-1) is a minimal core.

correction.text: the Oran province not under French control: 'France recognized Abdelkader as the sovereign of territories in Oran province not under French control' (Treaty of Desmichels)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Oranais region without the 30 km around French-held Oran (166 cells, about 42 k km2). The conquest page does not name the towns France held in 1834 (Arzew and Mostaganem are not on it); Tlemcen is occupied by Clauzel in January 1836. The Emirate page lists the provinces (Titteri/Medea, Miliana, Tlemcen, Mascara, Sahara/Laghouat, Mejdana/Setif, Ziban/Biskra, Jibal/Bouira) without dates, so only the Oran province is drawn before the Treaty of Tafna.

correction.text: 'approximately two thirds of Algeria': the provinces of Oran, Koléa, Médéa, Tlemcen and Algiers, without Constantine, as the Cliopatria 1836 remainder minus the Constantinois

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's 1836 'Regency of Algiers' remainder (196,606 km2) without the Constantinois region (498 of 743 cells, 67 per cent, against the page's 'approximately two thirds'). France kept its major ports. The page gives no frontier lines, only that the treaty defined 'the limits of its dominion' in the provinces of Oran and Algiers; the Iron Gates passage of late 1839 broke it.

correction.text: the unoccupied interior in the renewed war: the Cliopatria 1840 remainder (182,085 km2) without the Constantinois

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 497 cells. Abdelkader renewed the jihad in late 1839 (conquest page); Bugeaud replaced Valee in December 1840 with a scorched-earth strategy. Mejdana (Setif) and Ziban (Biskra), two of the Emirate's provinces on its page, lie partly in the Constantinois and are not added without a date. Tagdemt's fall is undated on the Emirate page.

correction.text: the unoccupied interior, shrinking: the Cliopatria 1842 remainder (163,274 km2) without the Constantinois

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 424 cells. The conquest page has the raid on the Smala in 1843 (more than 5,000 fighters and the war chest), the Sahara expedition from Biskra in March 1844 and the Kabylia campaign of 1845-1846, which ended Abdelkader's influence in the east; the Treaty of Tangier of 1844 outlawed the Emir in Morocco. Cliopatria's remainder stops in 1845, so 1846-1847 have no drawn land.

ledger.note: 27 November 1832: the Emirate of Abdelkader is established. The infobox gives the establishment as 27 November 1832 and the state rose with 'the allegiance of the people of Algeria' to resist the French conquest; Mascara is the capital. The page gives no territory.

region.text: the Oran province outside French-held Oran, recognised as Abdelkader's

ledger.note: 26 February 1834: the Treaty of Desmichels. 'France recognized Abdelkader as the sovereign of territories in Oran province not under French control'; the treaty did not require him to recognize French rule. The date is the Emirate page's (the conquest page gives only 1834); the extent of the Oran province is the researcher's reading.
1835: the capital moves from Mascara to Tagdemt. Infobox capitals: Mascara (1832-1835), then Tagdemt (1835-1847).

region.text: Tlemcen and the western Oran province

ledger.note: January 1836: Clauzel occupies Tlemcen. 'Clauzel occupied Tlemcen in January 1836' (the Treaty of Desmichels did not stop the war): the first French ground taken from the Emirate.

region.text: Tlemcen and the western Oran province

ledger.note: 30 May 1837: the Treaty of Tafna. General Bugeaud and the Emir signed it on 30 May 1837; the page gives the place of signing nowhere.

region.text: the interior beyond the Oran province: Titteri, the Algiers hinterland and the rest of the two thirds of Algeria

ledger.note: 30 May 1837: France recognises 'approximately two thirds of Algeria' as Abdelkader's, in exchange for his recognising French sovereignty; the provinces of Oran, Koléa, Médéa, Tlemcen and Algiers are named, France keeps its major ports and Constantine is taken by France on 13 October 1837. Bugeaud 'effectively recognized Abd al-Qadir's control over much of the interior' (conquest page).

region.text: the interior of the Algiers and Oran provinces fought over from 1839

ledger.note: Late 1839: the war resumes. French troops marched through the Iron Gates defile, which Abdelkader claimed under the treaty; he alleged a breach and renewed the call to jihad, and his 1839 Mitidja campaign was routed at Oued El Alleug. The page gives the year, not a month.

region.text: the interior, no longer held by the Emir

ledger.note: 1846: the fighting ends in the interior. The Kabylia campaign of 1845-1846, per the page, routed Ahmed at Tizi Ouzou and destroyed his forces near Issers, ending Abdelkader's influence in the east; Cliopatria's French Algeria row takes the whole country in 1846. The Emir himself held out until December 1847, so the date is a de facto end of the Emirate's ground.

region.text: the interior, which the French row draws from 1846

ledger.note: 1846: the last of the Emirate's ground passes to French Algeria. The year is Cliopatria's (French Algeria 48,573 km2 in 1842-1845 and 211,876 km2 from 1846); the conquest page gives the Smala raid of 1843, the Sahara expedition of 1844 and the Kabylia campaign of 1845-1846, none of which closes the matter.

region.text: no ground left: the Emir's surrender

ledger.note: 23 December 1847: Abd al-Qadir surrenders. The infobox gives the surrender as 23 December 1847; he surrendered 'under terms that he be allowed to enter exile in the Middle East' and was held in France until 1852 (conquest page).

wars.name: Desmichels and Tafna phase of the French conquest of Algeria

zones.text: Tlemcen, occupied by Clauzel in January 1836

wars.outcome: The Treaty of Desmichels (26 February 1834) recognised Abdelkader in the Oran province; the Treaty of Tafna (30 May 1837) recognised him over 'approximately two thirds of Algeria' and left France its ports.
wars.note: Constantine was attacked by Clauzel in November 1836 and taken on 13 October 1837; it was not Abdelkader's.

wars.name: French conquest of Algeria, last phase

zones.text: the unoccupied interior of the Algiers and Oran provinces

wars.outcome: After the Iron Gates passage of late 1839 and Bugeaud's scorched-earth campaigns (from December 1840), the Smala was raided in 1843, Abdelkader's influence in the east was ended in 1845-1846 and he surrendered on 23 December 1847.
wars.note: The page does not give the fall of Tagdemt, Mascara and Tlemcen in 1841-1842 or the Battle of Isly (August 1844) and the Treaty of Lalla Maghnia (March 1845); the Emirate page is silent on them too.

wars.name: First Franco-Moroccan War
wars.outcome: The French used military means in 1844 to compel the sultan; the 1844 Treaty of Tangier had Morocco outlaw the Emir from its kingdom.
wars.note: The page gives neither the battle (Isly) nor a date for the treaty; no border of the Emirate moved.

certainty.note: The Treaty of Tafna 'defined the limits of its dominion' in the Oran and Algiers provinces according to a footnote, but no page gives a line; every frontier is approximate.

notes: Emirate of Abdelkader (af-02-f, a direct counterpart of the Regency of Algiers that no Cliopatria row covers). (1) All keyframes are new; they are read from Cliopatria's unoccupied remainder of Algeria, which Cliopatria labels 'Regency of Algiers' until 1845, and the regency-of-algiers dossier marks those shapes wrong for that reason. The Constantinois is left out because the Tafna page's two thirds exclude Constantine; Setif and Biskra (provinces 'Mejdana' and 'Ziban' on the Emirate page) are not added because no page dates them. (2) Pages are thin: the Emirate page gives the establishment (27 November 1832), capitals, the two treaty dates (26 February 1834 and 30 May 1837) and the surrender (23 December 1847) and is silent on the rest; no page opened gives the fall of Tagdemt, Mascara and Tlemcen (1841-1842), the Smala date (conquest page: 1843), Isly (August 1844) or Lalla Maghnia (March 1845). The 1846 loss and contest end are confidence 1 (Cliopatria's French Algeria row takes the whole country in 1846). (3) The Beylik of Constantine (Ahmed Bey; repulsed Clauzel in November 1836, fell 13 October 1837) and the Kabyle, Saharan and Titteri polities need dossiers or an owner; Titteri and Constantine are named successors of the Regency. (4) Wikidata id unknown (no Cliopatria row); the site's link is left null.
